findings.title: URLClassLoader loads and instantiates .class files from arbitrary local path or URL (dormant in this variant)
findings.code_excerpt: url = new File( this.getPath() ).toURI().toURL(); ... URLClassLoader cl = new URLClassLoader( new URL[] { url } ); c = cl.loadClass( this.getClassname() ); return c.newInstance();
findings.entry_point: Constructor args (path, classname). In this variant there is NO caller: grep for 'new ApoClassLoader|getMyClass' across all 79 files returns nothing outside the class itself. The intended entry point survives as a vestige: apoPongBeat/ApoPongBeatComponent.java:95-110 builds a JFileChooser filtered by new ApoFileFilter("class") 'zum Laden einer KI' (load an AI), but showOpenDialog() is never called anywhere.
findings.sink: Class.forName-equivalent loadClass() at line 73 followed by c.newInstance() at line 75 - arbitrary bytecode static initializer / constructor execution
findings.data_path: (if wired) user-chosen .class path -> setPath()/setClassname() -> getMyClass():65-68 picks File(path).toURI().toURL() when ApoConstants.B_APPLET==false, else new URL(path) (remote codebase) -> URLClassLoader -> loadClass -> newInstance
findings.attack_scenario: In sibling variants where the chooser is wired, a victim is social-engineered into opening an attacker-supplied .class as their 'AI'; its constructor executes with full desktop permissions. As shipped in ApoPongBeat, nothing calls it: step 1 would be to add a caller, which does not exist today.
findings.preconditions: Requires code that instantiates ApoClassLoader and passes attacker-influenced path/classname; absent in this variant. In applet mode (B_APPLET=true, set by apoPongBeat/ApoPongBeatApplet.java:28) the path is interpreted as a URL, enabling purely remote class loading.
findings.validation_plan: (1) Prove dormancy: `grep -rn "new ApoClassLoader\|getMyClass" src/` -> no hits. (2) Prove the primitive works if ever wired: compile Evil.java whose constructor writes ~/pwned.txt, place next to a harness calling new ApoClassLoader(dir,"Evil").getMyClass(); pwned.txt appears, confirming arbitrary execution with no integrity check.

findings.title: Highscore level/username/solution submitted over plain HTTP - to the WRONG game's endpoints (apoNotSoSimple), never called in this variant
findings.code_excerpt: url = new URL(ApoConstants.HIGHSCORE_SAVEPHP); ... String content = "levelname=" + URLEncoder.encode(...) + "&username=" + ... + "&level=" + URLEncoder.encode(String.valueOf(myLevel), "UTF-8"); printout.writeBytes(content);
findings.entry_point: save(byte[][][] level, ..., String username, ...) at line 69 and load() at line 141. Zero callers in this variant: `grep -rn "ApoHighscore|HIGHSCORE" --exclude ApoHighscore.java` returns nothing; apoPongBeat/game/* never touches scores beyond local ints (ApoPongBeatPanel.ballOnRacketGame, line 299-307).
findings.sink: Cleartext HTTP POST to http://www.apo-games.de/apoNotSoSimple/save_highscore.php (org/apogames/ApoConstants.java:25) and GET counterpart HIGHSCORE_GETPHP (ApoConstants.java:24)
findings.data_path: (if wired) UI action -> ApoHighscore.getInstance().save()/load() -> url.openConnection() over http:// (no TLS anywhere in the file) -> printout.writeBytes(content); load() then trusts response lines positionally into level/usernames/descriptions/solution lists (lines 170-183) with no validation
findings.attack_scenario: Network attacker (coffee-shop MITM or malicious DNS for apo-games.de) reads usernames/submitted solutions in transit and can serve crafted response lines that populate the game's highscore lists. Not exploitable in ApoPongBeat as shipped because save()/load() are unreachable dead clones.
findings.preconditions: B_ONLINE=true already holds by default (ApoConstants.java:16); missing precondition is any call site. Note the clone-and-own artifact: PongBeat hardcodes the *apoNotSoSimple* PHP paths, proving constants were copied wholesale between variants without adaptation.
findings.validation_plan: (1) Dormancy: grep shows no references. (2) Wire behavior: harness calls ApoHighscore.getInstance().load() with DNS pointed at a netcat listener; observe plaintext POST body 'Get=' and confirm the request goes to the apoNotSoSimple path despite running ApoPongBeat.

findings.title: Applet 'cookie' storage sends name/value pairs to codebase cookies.php over plain HTTP
findings.code_excerpt: String parametersAsString = "SET=&name=" + name + "&value=" + value; ... url = new URL(codebase + "cookies.php"); URLConnection con = url.openConnection(); ((HttpURLConnection) con).setRequestMethod("GET"); oStream.write(parameterAsBytes);
findings.entry_point: ApoHelp.saveData(URL codebase, String name, String value) (line 419) and loadData(String name) (line 446). No callers anywhere in this variant (grep across all 79 files).
findings.sink: HTTP request to <codebase>cookies.php with body containing name/value; loadData() returns the first response line unvalidated to the caller (line 465)
findings.data_path: (if wired) game state strings -> saveData/loadData -> openConnection on caller-supplied codebase URL -> cleartext write/read
findings.attack_scenario: MITM reads/modifies persisted game state ('cookies') in flight, or a malicious codebase harvests whatever name/value pairs are stored. Dead code here: no path constructs these calls.
findings.preconditions: Caller must exist and supply a codebase; none does in this variant. Also note the method-set-to-GET-with-output-stream quirk, which only works against servers tolerating GET bodies.
findings.validation_plan: Harness: ApoHelp.saveData(new URL("http://127.0.0.1:8000/"), "progress","level9") while running `nc -l 8000`; observe ASCII 'SET=&name=progress&value=level9' in cleartext. Then grep to reconfirm zero production callers.

findings.title: MD5 helper for highscore/validation-style hashing (unused in this variant)
findings.code_excerpt: MessageDigest lDigest = MessageDigest.getInstance("MD5"); lDigest.update(pInput.getBytes()); BigInteger lHashInt = new BigInteger(1, lDigest.digest()); return String.format("%1$032X", lHashInt);
findings.entry_point: public static ApoHelp.getMd5Digest(String). No callers in this variant (`grep -rn getMd5Digest` matches only its definition). In siblings this hashes level solutions for the online highscore flow (cf. ApoHighscore.solution field).
findings.sink: MD5 digest used as integrity/validation token
findings.data_path: (in siblings) solution string -> getMd5Digest -> submitted alongside level in save_highscore.php POST; server-side comparisons inherit MD5 collision/preimage weaknesses. No data reaches it in ApoPongBeat.
findings.attack_scenario: Where wired, a cheater generates colliding/crafted solution hashes to submit fake solves; network attacker forges hash+solution pairs since transport is also plaintext (see ApoPongBeat-02). Pure library function here.
findings.preconditions: None locally - it is a static utility; exploitability requires the sibling-variant wiring plus server-side reliance on the hash.
findings.validation_plan: Unit test confirms MD5 output format (e.g. getMd5Digest("") == known digest); grep confirms no call sites; mark as latent corpus-wide weakness rather than an active flaw in this build.

findings.title: LAN UDP broadcast accepted unauthenticated as game-server entry; hand-rolled binary parser (dead network stack carried from siblings)
findings.code_excerpt: bsock.receive(dpr); ... DataContainer dc = new DataContainer(data, false); ServerEntry se = new ServerEntry(dc.getNextString(), dpr.getAddress(), dc.getNextInt(), dc.getNextInt()); ... servers.add(se);
findings.entry_point: Any host on the LAN can send one UDP datagram to the browser port (DatagramSocket bound at line 76, receive at line 83). The whole org.apogames.network package (20 files, ~2300 lines incl. SimpleClient/SimpleServer) has zero imports/references from apoPongBeat.* or the rest of org.apogames.* in this variant - verified by grep for 'import org.apogames.network'.
findings.sink: Attacker-controlled name/port/client-count inserted into the server browser list; downstream SimpleClient.Sender (SimpleClient.java:157 `new Socket(server, port)`) would connect to attacker-chosen host:port
findings.data_path: UDP packet -> 2-byte outer length strip (lines 89-90) -> DataContainer custom TLV parser (DataContainer.java:80 msgType from bytes[2..3], typed getNextString/getNextInt) -> ServerEntry -> displayed/connectable server list. Parser robustness: DataContainerFactory.extractContainers (lines 22-27) trusts a 16-bit length field for arraycopy and throws RuntimeException on truncation.
findings.attack_scenario: (where wired, e.g. sibling ApoSoccer) Attacker broadcasts a forged packet from a laptop: victim's browser lists 'FastGameServer 10.0.0.5:1337'; joining routes game traffic and any future protocol-level trust to the attacker. Spoofed source IP is unnecessary since no authentication exists.
findings.preconditions: Package must be referenced by game code; in ApoPongBeat it is compiled-in but completely unwired, so no socket is ever opened (verified: no DatagramSocket/Socket usage outside org/apogames/network/).
findings.validation_plan: (1) Dormancy: grep proves no imports; run the game with tcpdump - no traffic. (2) Capability proof: harness starts new ServerBrowser(4445).startBrowser(); send UDP payload [lenHi,lenLo][containerLenHi,Lo][msgTypeHi,Lo][TYPE_STRING len]["EvilServer"][TYPE_INT port][TYPE_INT 0] via nc -u; log line 'ServerBrowser: Server EvilServer added!' confirms LAN spoof acceptance.

findings.title: Sound loader contains plain-HTTP fetch from apo-games.de behind a permanently-false flag
findings.entry_point: AudioPlayer.run() non-JAR applet branch. Doubly dead: guard constant `private final boolean BInJAR = true;` (line 19) makes lines 67-71 unreachable bytecode, AND the live branch (line 65) only loads classpath resources '/sounds/Piano_*.wav' registered in ApoSounds.loadSound via ApoPongBeatComponent.load() lines 60-75.
findings.sink: Cleartext download and parsing of audio data from attacker-interceptable URL
findings.data_path: playSound(name) -> ApoSounds.playSound (ApoSounds.java:24-27) -> new AudioPlayer(path,...).run() -> (dead branch) new URL(http://www.apo-games.de/apoPongBeat + path).openStream into javax.sound decoder
findings.attack_scenario: If the flag were flipped and applet-deployed, a MITM could serve malformed audio to the javax.sound parser seeking memory-corruption bugs, or track players. Currently impossible: javap shows the constant-folded branch; no network sound path exists.
findings.preconditions: BInJAR must be changed from final true and applet deployment used; both fail today.
findings.validation_plan: `javap -c org.apogames.sound.AudioPlayer | grep -A2 ldc` shows only the getResource path; run the desktop game under `lsof -i` and observe zero sockets during menu music playback.

categories_checked_and_absent: untrusted_deserialization - no java.io.ObjectInputstream/readObject anywhere in the tree

path_traversal - no file writes from untrusted names; ApoCopy.copyDirectory/copyFile exists (ApoCopy.java:27-74) but has zero callers; ApoIO.readLevel/writeLevel have no subclass in this variant so no save/level file is ever parsed
credential_or_secret_exposure - no passwords, keys, tokens or credentials in any file

resource_exhaustion - live game loops are bounded (balls/particles removed when invisible, ApoPongBeatPanel.thinkBalls/thinkParticles lines 320-336); the only unbounded-length parsers sit inside the unused network package (already covered by ApoPongBeat-05)

legacy_sandbox_assumption - applet entry point exists (ApoPongBeatApplet.java) and flips B_APPLET globals, but no security decision depends on sandbox guarantees; folded into preconditions of other findings
notes: Headline result: ApoPongBeat is an offline-only arcade pong variant, and every corpus-typical dangerous component is present but UNREFERENCED dead clone-and-own baggage - zero findings are reachable as shipped. Evidence base: all 79 .java files enumerated and swept with sink greps (defineClass/URLClassLoader/ObjectInputStream/MessageDigest/System.load/Runtime.exec/new URL/openConnection/Socket/FileInputStream/user.home/user.dir); ~30 files read line-by-line including all apoPongBeat.game logic (pure AWT rendering/math), org/apogames core, help, image, sound packages. Key dormancy proofs: (1) ApoClassLoader.getMyClass has no callers although the .class-AI filechooser skeleton survives in ApoPongBeatComponent.java:95-110; (2) ApoHighscore.save/load have no callers even though ApoConstants.B_ONLINE defaults true - and the URLs point at apoNotSoSimple endpoints, a copy-paste smoking gun for measuring flaw propagation via cloned constants; (3) org.apogames.network (20 files) is imported nowhere; (4) ApoIO has no subclass, so no custom level/save/replay parser (.cheat/.mar/.skunk etc.) is instantiated here; (5) main() ignores argv entirely (ApoPongBeatMain.java:18). For the product-line study: this variant shows how clone-and-own carries vulnerable surface into builds where it cannot fire - the risk materializes the moment a maintainer re-wires the chooser/highscore/network plumbing that sibling variants (e.g. ApoSoccer for the network stack, ApoNotSoSimple/Sudoku for highscores) actively use.
